items.label: Lava flows
items.quote: Molten rock (magma) that pours or oozes onto the Earth’s surface is called lava and forms lava flows.

items.label: Basalt lava
items.quote: low-silica basalt lava can form fast-moving (10 to 30 miles per hour) streams

items.label: Lava domes
items.quote: Dacite and rhyolite lavas often squeeze out of a vent to form irregular mounds called lava domes.

items.label: Sulfur dioxide
items.quote: Other common volcanic gases are carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, hydrogen, and fluorine.

items.label: Carbon dioxide
items.quote: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air and can be trapped in low areas in concentrations that are deadly to people and animals.

items.label: Mudflows
items.quote: Mudflows or debris flows composed mostly of volcanic materials on the flanks of a volcano are called lahars.

items.label: Rock debris
items.quote: Some lahars contain so much rock debris (60 to 90% by weight) that they look like fast-moving rivers of wet concrete.
